Custom AI chips will outship GPUs by 2027.

That is J.P. Morgan's forecast: 12.5 million custom chips against 10.9 million GPUs. Yet the startups raising record sums may capture the smallest share
of it.

To see why, start with how AI chips are bought.

HOW THE MARKET WORKS

A GPU is a general-purpose chip. Nvidia designs it to run almost any AI workload and sells it to everyone. That flexibility made Nvidia the default
supplier, at a premium price.

A custom chip, or ASIC, is built for one buyer's workloads. Google's TPU is the best-known example.

The hyperscaler sets the design, and a partner such as Broadcom turns it into a manufacturable chip and brings it through production at TSMC.

Traditional banks are blocking AI agents from customer accounts. It’s an admission that the biggest players in banking don’t understand the next five years. And, it's a bad security policy. 


Mercury is building for founders that want to use agents securely. Our new Agent Controls page in the Mercury app shows every agent connected to your account, what it’s allowed to do, a record of activity, and lets you cut it off at any time in seconds.


Blocking agents is the opposite of a good security policy. Founders are already using agents, so trying to block them only pushes people to share a login with their agent or let it drive their browser with few guardrails and no record of what it did.
